reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically problematic because Cu has negligible solubility in refractory BCC elements and would likely form embrittling intermetallics or macroscopic soft phases at grain boundaries, undermining strength and energy release rather than enhancing ductility.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with a well-defined falsification criterion based on quantitative mechanical and microstructural comparisons, though the 20% improvement threshold is somewhat arbitrary.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is of limited use because the proposed dopant (Cu) is a poor choice for refractory alloys, and the mechanism of grain-boundary precipitates promoting sliding is more likely to cause embrittlement than ductility in this class of materials.
